title: New Sunscreen Ingredient Finally Approved in the U.S.!
summary:
Great news for sun lovers! The U.S. just approved a new sunscreen ingredient called bemotrizinol (say: beh-moh-TRIZ-eh-nol). It's the first new sunscreen chemical allowed in 20 years. This is exciting because bemotrizinol is really good at blocking the sun's aging rays, called UVA1. Those rays go deep into your skin and can make it wrinkly and spotted over time. Current U.S. sunscreens mostly block UVB rays that cause sunburns, but they're not as great against UVA1.

Bemotrizinol has other perks too. It's more stable than other sunscreen chemicals, so it doesn't break down as fast in sunlight. That means you might not need to reapply it as often. Plus, it's a big molecule, so it's less likely to soak through your skin into your blood. The FDA says it's safe and effective. Dr. Tanya Hathaway, a skin doctor, says, 'I think we should all be super excited.' She notes that Europe has used it for over 25 years, and it's also approved in Japan, Canada, and Australia.

You might see sunscreens with bemotrizinol on shelves after August 9. But remember, sunscreen isn't the only way to stay safe. Wearing long sleeves, hats, and sunglasses, and staying in the shade are great low-tech options. As Dr. Jennifer Stein says, 'The more clothing you're wearing, the less you have to depend on sunscreen.' So, get ready to enjoy the sun—safely!
why_it_matters: Protecting your skin from sun damage now can help you stay healthy and avoid painful sunburns and early wrinkles when you're older.

background_read: Sunscreen works by using chemicals or minerals that scatter or absorb the sun's damaging ultraviolet (UV) light before it can harm the skin.
UVA1 rays are known as 'aging rays' because they reach deeper skin layers and can break down collagen, causing wrinkles.

In the U.S., sunscreen ingredients are treated like over-the-counter drugs, so the FDA must carefully check their safety before they are allowed—which is why it took 20 years for a new one to be approved.

WHAT: A new sunscreen ingredient, bemotrizinol, was approved in the U.S. after 20 years
WHERE: The approval is for use in the U.S., but it has been sold in Europe, Japan, Canada, and Australia for years
WHY: Because it's very good at blocking aging UVA1 rays, is stable, and is safe for skin

perspectives.description: Dermatologists are excited because this ingredient fills a gap in U.S. sun protection, giving people stronger defense against skin aging and sun damage.
Some people worry about putting chemicals on children's skin, but the FDA's thorough tests and long use in other countries help show it is safe.
A sunscreen that doesn't break down quickly means less hassle reapplying, making it easier to stay protected during long days at the beach or playing sports.
